why: Unauthorised geofence modification can enable restricted-airspace entry and propagate into flight authorisation decisions.
Poisoned shared operational data can simultaneously corrupt mandatory services, compromise decisions and create widespread collision hazards.
Manipulated weather and traffic feeds can produce unsafe routing and undermine mandatory traffic-information services.
Tampered audit evidence undermines incident reconstruction, accountability and mandatory recorded-data retention obligations.
Compromised API credentials enable scalable operational-data exfiltration, exposing sensitive flight information and downstream services.
Database compromise can corrupt flight records, expose operational data and degrade multiple safety-relevant services.
Compromised regulatory audit records obstruct enforcement, accountability and compliance verification, with persistent governance consequences.
Regulatory ambiguity can undermine cybersecurity governance across every layer, indirectly weakening safety and compliance obligations.
Strategic document theft provides adversarial intelligence and compromises deployment confidentiality without an identified direct safety pathway.
GNSS spoofing or jamming can directly compromise aircraft positioning, navigation and restricted-airspace avoidance.
C2 disruption during BVLOS operations can cause loss of control, fail-safe behaviour and aircraft collision.
Persistent flight-controller compromise can subvert aircraft behaviour, propagate through telemetry and create direct crash hazards.
Power disruption or BMS manipulation can disable ground operations or cause mid-flight battery depletion and uncontrolled landing.
Manipulated altitude, inertial or positioning measurements can corrupt flight decisions and directly contribute to aircraft crashes.
Physical sabotage of vertiport controls can compromise landing operations and expose aircraft and people to safety hazards.
Trusted supply-chain compromise can distribute persistent malicious firmware across fleets and undermine aircraft safety systemically.
Identity spoofing enables unaccountable operations, undermining operator authentication, registration integrity and regulatory oversight.
False aircraft positions can conceal real traffic conflicts, undermine situational awareness and defeat collision-avoidance functions.
Authorisation bypass can permit illegal or conflicting flights and directly compromise mandatory airspace access controls.
Gateway flooding can simultaneously disable mandatory services across the operational volume and interrupt service continuity.
Falsified geofences can authorise unsafe routing into restricted airspace and compromise airspace compliance.
